positioning: The teddy bear in a tweed coat. Britain's sturdy, dignified original.
story: The British Shorthair is the founding cat of Britain, descended from the working cats the Romans are said to have carried to the island to guard their grain. For centuries it was simply the British street and farm cat, before fanciers turned it into the plush, round-faced breed seen today.

It is built like a brick. A broad round head, full cheeks, big copper eyes, and a stocky cobby body sit under a dense, crisp coat that stands away from the skin. The blue-grey version, the British Blue, is so iconic that many people think it is the only color.

The temperament is famously easygoing. British Shorthairs are calm, dignified, and a little reserved, affectionate without being clingy. They will keep you company from across the room rather than demanding a lap, and they tolerate being left alone better than most.

Their plush looks have made them cultural icons. The breed is often named as the inspiration for the Cheshire Cat and for Puss in Boots. Easy to live with and slow to anger, the British Shorthair is one of the most popular cats in Britain and a steady climber in America.

The British Shorthair is one of the easiest cats to live with. It is calm, undemanding, and content to keep you company from its own chosen spot, tolerating time alone better than most and rarely making a fuss. It is not a natural lap cat and often prefers to sit beside you rather than on you.

Two things need watching. The dense coat sheds and wants regular brushing, more in spring, and the breed loves its food and gains weight easily, so portions matter. Like many breeds it can carry the heart condition HCM, and the kidney condition PKD appears in some lines, so good breeders test.

Descended from the rodent-catching cats of farms and streets, said to trace back to cats brought by the Romans.
Independent and undemanding, it likes company without needing a lap. The dense coat needs regular brushing, and the breed can run heavy, so watch the diet.
A short, dense, crisp coat in many colors, with the blue-grey British Blue the signature look.
Often cited as the model for the Cheshire Cat and Puss in Boots, and one of the most popular breeds in the United Kingdom.
Brush the dense coat regularly and watch the waistline. Independent and tidy, it suits owners who want an easygoing companion.
Can carry the heart condition HCM and, in some lines, the kidney condition PKD, so favor screened breeders and keep meals measured.
days: The British Shorthair is said to descend from cats the Romans brought for grain.
For centuries it was just the farm and street cat. Then fanciers took notice.
The blue-grey British Blue is famous, but the breed comes in many colors.
One sock, one paw, and no explanation. The sock now belongs to the cat.
A calm cat watches the snow and learns that it will fall without any help.
Ask which cat tested the snow first. The answer is always the sturdiest one.
Even a dignified cat will leap for a feather. It just will not admit it.
last_walk:
The fire is low and the house smells of woodsmoke and wool.
The British Shorthair has watched the snow, claimed a sock, and tested the doorstep. Now it settles into the basket by the hearth, round face on a folded plaid, a teddy bear in a tweed coat. The first sleeper of the night.
cap: Britain's plush original, a steady top-ten cat (CFA)
